stories.headline: Brewers rout the Rays 10-1 in Game 3 and are one win from their first World Series title
stories.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 Monday night at Tropicana Field and lead the World Series 3-0. Jackson Chourio went 4 for 5 and bookended an eight-run fifth inning, which Brice Turang opened with a two-out, two-run single. Rookie left-hander Robert Gasser threw one-hit ball and faced the minimum through six innings, the first starter to do that in a World Series game since Curt Schilling in 2001 and the first lefty since Sandy Koufax in 1965. Milwaukee piled up 16 hits off ALCS MVP Freddy Peralta and five relievers to win its eighth straight game, tying the record for a single postseason, while thousands of traveling Brewers fans cheered behind the visitors' dugout. Of 43 teams to fall behind 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series, only the 2004 Red Sox came back. Game 4 is Tuesday night in St. Petersburg.

stories.headline: Israel votes today in its first election since Oct. 7, and Netanyahu's future could take weeks to settle
stories.summary: Israelis are voting Tuesday in a tight election that will shape their next government, the first since Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attack and with the country still fighting in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria after two rounds of direct conflict with Iran. Right-leaning pollsters give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc the edge, while left-leaning pollsters favor the opposing “change” bloc, and most show neither side reaching a 61-seat majority in the 120-seat Knesset. That could mean drawn-out coalition talks, a minority government or even a do-over. Netanyahu argues only he can govern without Arab parties and finish the wars, especially against Iran. President Trump endorsed him last week and warned that if Israel has “the wrong Leader,” America would have to finish the Iran job itself and is “not inclined to do so.” Netanyahu's campaign slogan is “Either right wing or Palestine, either right wing or a nuclear bomb.”

stories.headline: U.K. charges two men in the alleged Iran-linked plot against RAF Fairford, the base U.S. bombers used to strike Iran
stories.summary: British prosecutors on Tuesday charged two London men, Mohmed Abdulkarim and Nouman Essghir, both 24, under the 2023 National Security Act in connection with last month's incident near RAF Fairford in western England. Abdulkarim is accused of assisting a foreign intelligence service, and Essghir of approaching a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to U.K. safety. Five men were first detained near the base on Sept. 27, when nearby residents were evacuated and police found gasoline in three vans parked near an entrance, but no explosives. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said Iran “played a part,” and the U.S. Air Force pulled all of its B-1 bombers from Fairford, which had launched strikes on Iran during the war. Iran's embassy denies any link. Six other men, all in their 20s, remain free on bail while the investigation continues.

stories.headline: Valkyries beat the Dream 64-55 in Game 5 and are one win from a WNBA title in only their second season
stories.summary: Kiah Stokes had 13 points, eight rebounds and three blocks as the Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 64-55 Monday night at Chase Center to take a 3-2 lead in the WNBA Finals. Veronica Burton added 13 points and eight rebounds, and former Dream guard Tiffany Hayes, who came out of retirement two years ago, scored 12. Leading scorer Gabby Williams shot 3 for 14, but the Valkyries forced 17 turnovers that led to 21 points. Angel Reese was held to seven points with 15 rebounds and was called for three offensive fouls. The teams set a WNBA Finals record for the lowest-scoring first half, with Golden State up 25-22 at the break before pulling away. Stokes has three or more blocks in six straight games, tying Lisa Leslie's 2003 postseason record. Game 6 is Thursday at 12:30 p.m. EDT in Atlanta, an unusual time because an NBA game has the arena that night. A Game 7 would be Saturday in San Francisco.

stories.headline: 13 charged with running stolen cars and trucks through El Paso to Mexican cartels, including armored SUVs
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors in West Texas say a cross-border pipeline moved vehicles stolen from private owners and big rental-car companies through El Paso into Mexico, where cartels used them in their day-to-day operations. Thirteen people face charges of interstate transportation of stolen property, which carries up to 10 years in federal prison, in a case called Operation Southbound Takedown. Investigators have recovered 29 vehicles worth about $1.14 million, including an armored SUV and an armored pickup. Eleven of those charged are U.S. citizens and two are Mexican citizens. HSI's El Paso chief said these “are not isolated property crimes,” and U.S. Attorney Justin Simmons warned that people driving stolen vehicles south for a “quick buck” are helping cartels with human smuggling, extortion, drug trafficking “and even murder.” “You are now on notice,” he said.

stories.headline: Feds say 405 noncitizens voted in Washington state elections, casting more than 1,500 ballots, and call it the “tip of the iceberg”
stories.summary: Neil Floyd, the acting U.S. attorney for the Western District of Washington, said Monday that investigators have identified 405 people they believe are not U.S. citizens who voted in Washington elections, casting more than 1,500 ballots over multiple elections. Federal officials sent the names to state election officials and asked them to set those ballots aside until eligibility is checked. Floyd said he is confident “thousands” of noncitizens have voted, though he did not give a statewide count, and the 1,500 ballots span several decades. DHS investigators matched public voter lists against federal records one person at a time, because Washington has refused to share its full voter database with identifying information. Floyd said his office will prosecute illegal voters and anyone who knowingly helps them. The Justice Department has also sued California to hold mailed ballots from more than 20,000 voters it flagged as likely noncitizens.

stories.headline: Tesla's Cybercab line now builds robotaxis faster than Tesla can put them on the road
stories.summary: Tesla's Cybercab line in Texas is running so fast that it is outpacing deployments, vehicle engineering VP Lars Moravy said in a new Munro Live deep dive. “We don't run every day because the line can run so fast,” he said. The “unboxed” process builds front, rear, side and center modules separately before they meet on a short final line with just 25 automated stations, a fifth to a tenth of what a Model Y needs. The line is about 78% automated, the goal is one Cybercab every 10 seconds, and there's no paint shop, since exterior panels get their color inside the molding machine. The two-seater is designed to run at least 500,000 miles. Its 4680 battery pack sits in a steel enclosure with modules that can be swapped one at a time, and Tesla's battery director graded it an A minus, versus a D for the Model Y structural pack. Deployment, not production, is now the bottleneck.

stories.headline: Cowboys beat the Eagles 38-21 on Monday Night Football, handing Philadelphia its fifth straight loss
stories.summary: Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes, two to CeeDee Lamb, and Javonte Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards as Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-21 at Lincoln Financial Field. Brandon Aubrey opened with a 55-yard field goal, the teams traded leads, and the Cowboys led 20-14 at halftime after Prescott hit Lamb and George Pickens for scores. Tanner McKee's 4-yard pass to rookie Makai Lemon briefly put the Eagles ahead in the third quarter, but Prescott answered with a 16-yard touchdown to Lamb and ran in the two-point conversion. Aubrey added another field goal, DeMarvion Overshown intercepted McKee, and Williams closed it with a 2-yard run. Prescott finished 15 of 27 for 212 yards with no interceptions. Dallas is 3-4, and the Eagles fall to 2-5, with fans already calling for a quarterback change.

stories.headline: Blue Planet III keeps its murky, imperfect shots on purpose to prove no AI was used, with Attenborough narrating at 100
stories.summary: David Attenborough, now 100, is back to narrate the BBC's Blue Planet III, and the producers say not a single frame was made with generative AI. “It's all real photography,” BBC factual commissioning head Jack Bootle said. Executive producer Elizabeth White said the crew used to cut shots with plankton-clouded water or a stray boat or buoy in frame, but now keeps those imperfections because AI “makes us want to be even more authentic.” The series was filmed over four years across five oceans with new gear, including a mini dome camera that follows octopuses, a deep-sea selfie stick, lasers to light creatures in darkness, leg-mounted scooters and splash drones. A “stonefish” camera, billed as the world's first underwater CCTV, caught dolphins using sea sponges to plug holes in coral and trap fish. Other scenes show a grouper communicating with another species and about 200,000 crabs feeding in formation.

stories.headline: Acer's $1,300 Predator Atlas 8 gaming handheld comes to the U.S. Nov. 1, and the first preorders already sold out
stories.summary: Acer's Predator Atlas 8, a Windows 11 gaming handheld first shown at Computex 2026, goes on sale in the U.S. on Nov. 1, only at Best Buy, for $1,300. That's far more than a Steam Deck or ROG Ally, but Acer says the first round of preorders sold out last week, and online orders reopen when it hits stores. It runs on Intel's new Arc G3 Extreme chip and has an 8-inch 1920x1200 touchscreen with a 120Hz variable refresh rate, an 80Wh battery, two cooling fans, dual-mode triggers and TMR joysticks that resist drift. Because it runs Windows, it plays existing Steam and Xbox Game Pass libraries and can be docked to a bigger screen. Android Authority says that at that price it needs to run games noticeably better than rivals, not just run them.

stories.headline: Donnie Iris, the Pittsburgh rock legend behind “Ah! Leah!” and “Love Is Like a Rock,” dies at 83
stories.summary: Donnie Iris, the Ellwood City, Pennsylvania, singer behind “Ah! Leah!,” has died at 83, a former bandmate said Monday. He was diagnosed with bladder cancer shortly after a sold-out 80th birthday show in 2023, canceled some dates, then returned to the stage, and he only announced his retirement this month after a Sept. 28 show at Citizens Live at The Wylie. Iris first hit No. 1 in 1970 writing and singing “The Rapper” with the Jaggerz. After joining Wild Cherry in 1978 he met Mark Avsec, and the two formed Donnie Iris & The Cruisers, whose “Back On The Streets” album produced “Ah! Leah!” A reviewer's “new king of cool” line became the follow-up album “King Cool,” with “Love Is Like A Rock” and “My Girl.” The band toured with Journey, Foreigner, Bon Jovi, Loverboy, Joan Jett and Hall & Oates. Pittsburgh Mayor Corey O'Connor said Iris “was part of the soundtrack of our city.”

stories.headline: Jay-Z will headline the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI halftime show at SoFi Stadium on Valentine's Day
stories.summary: Apple and the NFL announced Monday night that Jay-Z, billed with the stylized spelling “JAŸ-Z,” will headline the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles. The game is on Sunday, Feb. 14, 2027, so the show lands on Valentine's Day. In the U.S. the Super Bowl airs on ABC and ESPN, and the halftime show usually starts between about 8:00 and 8:15 p.m. Eastern. No other performers have been announced yet. Apple has sponsored the halftime show since 2022, and the announcement came with a short teaser video on Apple Music's YouTube channel.

stories.headline: Manhunt in Tennessee for a convicted killer who went over a prison fence in his uniform and stole a flatbed truck
stories.summary: Tennessee authorities are searching for Jacob Allen Morley, 28, a convicted murderer serving life who escaped from the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville. He was reported missing at 11:30 p.m. Sunday, and security video shows he breached the perimeter fence in his prison uniform. By 1 a.m. Monday he is accused of stealing a white Ford F-350 flatbed truck in the town of about 3,500, near the Mississippi River and the Missouri line, about 100 miles north of Memphis. The TBI put him on its most-wanted list and asked residents to check doorbell and trail cameras. Morley is 5-foot-11 and 240 pounds; a reward of up to $2,500 is offered, and anyone who sees him should call 911 or 1-800-TBI-FIND. Court records say he shot co-worker Cody Birchfield in the back of the head in 2022 and hid the body in a metal box under his home. He was convicted in February 2025.

stories.headline: Halide's first iPhone Duo update turns the half-open foldable into a waist-level viewfinder camera
stories.summary: Camera app Halide is one of the first third-party apps to build specifically for the iPhone Duo. Developer Lux Optics released an update with separate shooting modes for each of the foldable's three poses: folded, partly open and fully open. One option lets you move the camera controls when the phone is open or half-open, and in the partly open position the Duo works much like a classic waist-level viewfinder, held low and looked down into. The update is available now for Halide Mark III users, and Lux Optics says more Duo features are coming. Engadget notes that app support was one of the big open questions in its Duo review, and Halide, once reportedly an Apple acquisition target, answered it quickly.

stories.headline: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General, saying it charged more at the register than its shelf tags for years
stories.summary: The Federal Trade Commission and 20 states sued Dollar General on Monday, accusing the 21,000-store chain of routinely charging shoppers more at checkout than the prices on its shelves, tags and ads, “extracting millions of dollars in unlawful overcharges.” The complaint, filed in federal court in Tennessee, where Dollar General is based, says the pattern lasted years, hit thousands of stores and drew thousands of consumer complaints. The FTC's consumer protection chief said the company “betrayed the trust” of shoppers who are already stretching paychecks. Dollar General says its goal is 100% price accuracy, that occasional discrepancies happen at any retailer and are corrected for customers, and that it has improved its processes. It said the FTC demanded money “orders of magnitude larger” than any realistic estimate and that it will fight the suit. The case seeks an injunction plus money and other relief.

stories.headline: Marty Friedman on quitting Megadeth mid-tour in 2000: “The decision was not difficult. Carrying it out was”
stories.summary: Former Megadeth guitarist Marty Friedman told VRP Rocks he never doubted his decision to leave the band in 2000, but regrets how he did it, three months into the European leg of the “Risk” tour. “I was just not the coolest person at that point. It was very selfish of me,” he said, adding that he “made good with Mustaine and the band years after that, but there were a lot of things I was not proud of.” Friedman joined in 1990 and played on “Rust in Peace” and “Countdown to Extinction” in the classic lineup with Dave Mustaine, David Ellefson and Nick Menza. Asked about wanting to move past metal, he said metal is “deep in my foundation,” but “you can't be bound by a genre forever,” and that the whole band wanted Led Zeppelin- and Rolling Stones-style longevity. “It wasn't just me,” he said. Earlier this month Mustaine praised Friedman for owning how he handled the exit.

stories.headline: Fujifilm's Instax Mini Evo 2 hybrid camera gets a giant touchscreen, a film-lever print control and a $289.95 price
stories.summary: Fujifilm announced the Instax Mini Evo 2, a refresh of its hybrid camera that shoots digitally and prints only the shots you choose on Instax Mini film. It keeps the retro silver body, a top dial for 10 color film looks, a lens ring for creative effects like double exposures and light leaks, and a print lever that works like an old film-advance lever. The big change is on the back, where a touchscreen fills nearly the whole camera and shows a little beyond the frame. There's also a new sensor, a macro mode and quick exposure compensation. Digital Camera World's reviewer calls it “way more fun than a cheap camera ought to be,” but notes there's no viewfinder, the screen can be hard to see in bright sun, and the battery is rated for about 90 shots. It also prints phone photos through the Instax app. It costs $289.95, up from about $234 for the original, and ships at the end of November.

stories.headline: LEGO Technic's new Ducati Desmo450 MX motocrosser has a chain-driven engine, working suspension and 457 pieces
stories.summary: Ducati and LEGO have released a second Technic collaboration, set 42238, a 457-piece model of the Desmo450 MX Factory, the race-ready version of Ducati's first motocross bike. Spin the rear wheel and a chain drives the engine's moving parts. The handlebars steer, the front and rear suspension compress and rebound, and the body panels come off to show the Technic frame underneath. Red-and-black Ducati Corse graphics, No. 222 plates and gold fork legs match the real bike, and a Ducati stand is included. The model, for ages 10 and up, is about 31 cm long and 19 cm tall, and the LEGO Builder app has 3D instructions. It's on sale now for £44.99 in the UK and A$89.99 in Australia. The partnership began in 2020 with the Technic Panigale V4 R, and both models will be shown with a full-size Desmo450 at Lucca Comics & Games in Italy from Oct. 28 to Nov. 1.

stories.headline: James Comey charged a third time, now over an alleged 2016 leak to a reporter — by prosecutors' filing, not a grand jury
stories.summary: Former FBI Director James Comey has been charged with transmitting national defense information and conspiracy to transmit it, the third federal case the Trump administration has brought against him. A filing unsealed Monday says Comey directed FBI staff to talk with a New York Times reporter about accuracy problems in an October 2016 Reuters story on Yahoo email surveillance, and that this illegally passed along classified information. Prosecutors used a criminal information rather than a grand jury indictment. Comey's lawyers, who moved to dismiss 10 days ago, argue the case is time-barred because the 10-year limit required an indictment by Oct. 5, 2026. Comey called the case “an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice” and said, “I'm still innocent. I'm still not afraid of these people.” His first case was dismissed, and a separate April indictment in North Carolina is still pending.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: early voting’s final week at the library, a Town Hall Halloween parade for preschoolers, and a Hillcrest update
stories.summary: Early voting runs its final week in the Trumbull Library Community Room, 33 Quality St., from Monday, Oct. 26, through Sunday, Nov. 1. Hours are 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., extended to 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Tuesday and Thursday. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. On Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 10 and 11:30 a.m., Town Hall staff host a costume parade and trick-or-treating past decorated office doors for registered Trumbull kids ages 0 to 5. Each session is limited to 20 children. That evening the Hillcrest Middle School Building Committee gets project updates and the EMS Commission reviews vehicles, staffing and plans for Trumbull EMS’s 50th anniversary. The Conservation Commission meets Wednesday on tree rules and a spring 2027 tree giveaway.
